_note: Rules for tools/scan.py, modelled on the open-source tool named in 'like'. Python regex syntax. Within a group the first matching rule wins for a line, so specific rules come before generic ones. A rule marked secret has its match redacted in every output. People change this file, agents never.

rules.title: Live payment API key (PayGrid) in code
rules.fix: Read the key from the environment (os.environ) as main does. The key is exposed: a person rotates it at PayGrid (Tier 2).

rules.title: AWS access key id in code
rules.fix: Read credentials from the environment or a secrets manager. A person deactivates the key in AWS (Tier 2).

rules.title: Private key in the repository
rules.fix: Remove the key from the repository. A person replaces the key pair (Tier 2).

rules.title: Hard-coded password, token or secret
rules.fix: Read the value from the environment or a secrets manager. A person rotates it if it was real (Tier 2).

rules.title: SQL query built from a variable (SQL injection)
rules.fix: Pass values as query parameters, for example cur.execute("... WHERE customer_ref = %s", (customer_ref,)).

rules.title: Command run through a shell
rules.fix: Pass the command as a list without shell=True, and never build it from input.

rules.title: eval or exec on dynamic input
rules.fix: Remove eval and exec; parse input explicitly, for example with json.loads.

rules.title: Unsafe deserialisation with pickle
rules.fix: Never unpickle data from outside; use JSON.

rules.title: TLS certificate check turned off
rules.fix: Keep certificate checks on (verify=True is the default).

rules.title: Downloads a script and runs it (download and execute)
rules.fix: Remove the line: ship scripts with the release, never fetch and run code at deploy time. Block the download host (Tier 1).

rules.title: Runs an encoded payload
rules.fix: Remove the payload and treat the push as malicious: on-call decides about the author's account.

rules.title: Crypto-miner pool address
rules.fix: Remove it: a miner in the code means the account or the build is compromised. On-call decides about the author's account.
